solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scotsman restricts fun one August

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the Scotsman's letters go around the rest

parts.note: Mac is a familiar name for a Scotsman
a jest is a bit of fun
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A Scotsman limits the amount of enjoyment one may have during the month of August.
explanation.walkthrough: August looks like the month, but here it is the adjective (capitalised only because it opens the definition at the end).
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means grand, dignified and imposing, a close synonym.

clue.text: Misfortune truly besets model after a day

indicators.note: after says the besetting construction follows the opening pair of letters
to beset is to surround, so the word for truly goes around the word for model

parts.note: very, as in 'the very man', means truly or really
to sit is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A sincere statement that a day's work disturbed a fashion model and brought bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Adversity is hardship or bad luck, a direct synonym of misfortune.

clue.text: Supply has to last, right away

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: to endure is to last or persist

explanation.surface: A store of provisions has to hold out, and quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'immediately' but splits: R is removed ('away') from the word for 'to last'.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is a literary verb meaning to endow or provide someone with a quality, so supply fits.

clue.text: Plague emptied industrial plant

parts.note: to plague is to torment

indicators.note: emptied means the word loses its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Pollution troubles a factory that has been cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'industrial plant' looks like a factory, but plant is the definition: a wildflower.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormentil is a small yellow-flowered herb of the rose family, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Tree planted in centre of volcanic crater

indicators.note: planted in says the tree's letters go inside the other letters
centre of picks the middle two letters of the word

parts.note: the alder is a tree that grows by water

explanation.surface: A sapling has been set into the middle of a volcano's crater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volcanic crater' looks like the definition, but volcanic only supplies its middle letters CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A caldera is a large basin formed when a volcano's summit collapses, a type of crater.

clue.text: I study boring books to impress

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the study goes inside the books

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that working through dull books is meant to make an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull; it means drilling through.
explanation.definitionFit: To indent is to make a dent or mark in a surface, i.e. to impress it.

clue.text: Nana's rheumatoid infection partly returned

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Granny's joint infection has partly come back.
explanation.walkthrough: Nana looks like granny; it is the British slang for a fool, and 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nana is British slang for a silly person or fool, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: One makes spirits calm in the middle of rough ride

indicators.note: in the middle of puts the word for calm inside the other letters
rough says the following word's letters are roughed up into a new order

parts.note: still means calm, motionless

explanation.surface: A medium raises ghosts and calms everyone during a bumpy journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges the ride into DIER. 'One makes spirits' suggests a medium; it is someone producing whisky or gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A distiller produces spirits such as whisky or gin by distillation.

clue.text: Fine clothes top of expenses for family member

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the word for fine wraps around the letter

parts.note: nice means fine or pleasant

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter, as this is a down clue

explanation.surface: Smart clothes eat up most of the budget for a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun but is the verb 'dresses', the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a relative.

clue.text: One who avoids commercial breaks always

indicators.note: breaks says the commercial cuts into the word for always

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
an ad is a commercial or advertisement

explanation.surface: A viewer who always dodges the advert breaks on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial breaks' reads as one phrase, but splits into AD plus the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An evader is a person who evades, i.e. dodges or avoids something.

clue.text: Irish province's city requiring name for church

indicators.note: name for church means the letters for name replace those for church

parts.note: Leicester is a city in the English Midlands
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irish province's chief city needs a new name for its church.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland, in the east, containing Dublin.

clue.text: Tail of golden retriever wags — that's cheeky

indicators.note: wags means moves to and fro, so the letters are shaken into a new order
tail of takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A golden retriever wagging its tail is being impudent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wags' is the anagram signal: N from golden plus RETRIEVER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreverent means showing a lack of respect, which is close to cheeky or impudent.

clue.text: Composer is left out

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is left out of the word

parts.note: lives means exists or is, as in 'he lives'

explanation.surface: A composer has been left out of the programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' must be swapped for LIVES before L is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer.

clue.text: Grain, or what you may do with grain, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the answer sounds like the phrase that precedes it

parts.words: what you may do with grain
parts.note: you might mill grain, i.e. 'mill it'

explanation.surface: A question about a cereal and what is done to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Millet is a small-seeded cereal crop, a type of grain.

clue.text: Rake it in, working with rebel

indicators.note: working means operating or in motion, so the letters are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel is busy raking in the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake it in' looks like an idiom for earning a lot; Rake alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute, immoral man, the same as a libertine.

clue.text: Animal is bound to stake first

indicators.note: first says the word for stake comes before the word for bound

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in poker before the deal
to lope is to run with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: An animal is certain to be tied to a post first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to stake' looks like 'tied to a post'; bound is LOPE and stake is ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a deer-like grazing mammal of Africa and Asia, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Animal breeders regularly entering shed

indicators.note: entering says the picked letters go inside the other word

parts.note: to shed is to cast off, as in threw off

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: Animal breeders keep going into the shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a hut but is the verb: THREW, as a horse throws a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree shrew is a small squirrel-like mammal of South-East Asia, an animal.

clue.text: Make jokes amiably or sarcastically?

parts.note: to pun is to make jokes by wordplay
gently means kindly or amiably

explanation.surface: A question of whether to joke kindly or with a sharp tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' sets up a contrast, but merely links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent remarks are sharply caustic, so speaking pungently is speaking cuttingly, as sarcasm is.

clue.text: Representative thus embraces Chuck with my backing

indicators.note: embraces says the word for thus goes around the other letters

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as exact

indicators.note: backing says the letters for chuck and my are read backwards

parts.note: to chuck is to lob or throw

explanation.surface: A deputy hugs Chuck while supporting me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a name but is the verb, to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Something symbolic stands for or represents something else, so it is representative.

clue.text: Two-time, filled by passion?

indicators.note: filled by says the word for passion goes inside the word for two-time

parts.note: to two-time is to deceive or double-cross, i.e. to con
heat means passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: Someone is unfaithful to a partner because they are consumed by passion.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: infidelity driven by passion, with the question mark flagging the double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unfaithful to a partner in the heat of an affair is exactly what two-timing describes.

clue.text: Rambling tirade by monarch

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the monarch
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A long-winded outburst delivered by the King or Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means beside here, so the monarch's letters sit next to the tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means wandering or roving, as in a knight errant, so it fits rambling.

clue.text: Boom box

definitions.meaning: a pole or ... on a ship, such as the one along the foot of a sail
to fight with the fists, as boxers do in practice

explanation.surface: A ghetto blaster, a boom box.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a ship's pole, and to spar is to box in practice.

clue.text: Opulent prince gets drunk

parts.note: a lush is a drunk, a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A wealthy prince gets intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Plush means luxurious and expensive-looking, close to opulent.

clue.text: Visionary — gullible sort providing material

parts.note: a seer is a prophet or visionary
a sucker is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: A prophet who is easily taken in supplies some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' could mean evidence; it is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a puckered cotton fabric, a kind of material.

clue.text: Kid had influence, so they say

indicators.note: so they say signals that the answer sounds like the word for had influence

parts.note: swayed means influenced

explanation.surface: A child was persuaded, or so people report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child; it is the leather, kidskin.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is leather from young goats, and suede is a soft napped leather, often kidskin.

clue.text: Police must restrain excited boy with bow

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the police letters go round the other letters

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
up means excited or stirred, as in 'het up'

explanation.surface: Officers must hold back an agitated youth carrying a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid, the Roman god of love, is depicted as a winged boy carrying a bow and arrows.

clue.text: Essential money to feed diminutive sort

indicators.note: to feed is to put food into, so the money goes inside the small one

parts.note: a runt is an undersized person or animal
a dime is a US ten-cent coin, money

explanation.surface: Money is needed to feed a small person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential' is a noun here: a basic element.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudiment is a basic principle or element, an essential.

clue.text: Name Peter Ustinov's first novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement
first takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: The actor Peter Ustinov's debut novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it is the anagram signal. Name means reputation here.
explanation.definitionFit: A good name is a good reputation; repute is the standing in which someone is held.

clue.text: Children learn about East Cheshire?

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to see is to learn or find out

explanation.surface: Children study the eastern part of the county of Cheshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire looks like the English county; it is the crumbly cheese of that name, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheshire is a named variety of cheese, so it is an example, indicated by the question mark.

clue.text: No manners? That includes lawyer at present

indicators.note: includes says the lawyer's letters go inside the other letters

parts.note: ways are habits or manners
a DA is a US district attorney, a lawyer

explanation.surface: Bad manners being covered by a lawyer at present.
explanation.walkthrough: DA is the American district attorney, a prosecuting lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means in the present age, at present.
